key_insight: Instead of using a fixed masking/corruption ratio for time-series masked reconstruction, the paper treats corruption level as a controllable degree of freedom and trains a Flow-Guided Neural Operator (FGNO) to learn representations that generalize across a continuum of corruption intensities. This yields more flexible and robust self-supervised features for time-series data.
problem_solved: Current time-series SSL methods use static, predetermined corruption levels (e.g., a fixed masking ratio), which limits adaptability and representation quality across different downstream tasks and noise regimes.
method: Introduce FGNO: a neural operator architecture that models the mapping between corrupted and original time-series across varying corruption levels (a continuous corruption-control input).
Use a flow-guided mechanism to steer corruption intensity during pretraining, exposing the encoder to a spectrum of difficulties rather than a single fixed mask ratio.
Train with a self-supervised reconstruction (or related) objective across the corruption continuum so learned representations are robust and transferable to diverse downstream tasks.
impact: By making corruption level a learned/control variable and training a neural operator over that continuum, practitioners get more adaptable, robust time-series representations that reduce sensitivity to mask hyperparameters and improve performance across varied downstream settings.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: FGNO block showing encoder, neural operator taking corruption-level input, and decoder/reconstruction head.
Continuum illustration: a slider or spectrum depicting corruption intensity from low to high with example time-series reconstructions along it.
Performance chart: downstream task accuracy/robustness vs. fixed-mask baselines across varied noise/masking regimes.
Ablation heatmap: effect of corruption scheduling and flow guidance on representation quality (or transfer performance).
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning via Flow-Guided Neural Operator on Time-Series Data
paper_authors: Duy Nguyen, Jiachen Yao, Jiayun Wang, Julius Berner, Animashree Anandkumar
